### Season outlook as written in the guide (p. 212)

A season with 10 or 11 wins in the regular season cannot be described as a disappointment, right? In Notre Dame’s case, it just might be. Perhaps calling it a “cupcake” schedule would be a little bit too critical, but it’s a “bundt cake” schedule at the very least. The Fighting Irish get a crack at Miami in a major revenge game at home on November 7 and that looks to be far and away the biggest test for the team. Obviously a lot of things can happen from a health standpoint, but Marcus Freeman and his staff have put together a spectacular roster. Freeman is 34-7 over the last three seasons. While Notre Dame gets to pick their schedule as an Independent, they’ve still been tested, facing 12 ranked teams in the regular season over that span. There’s a chance that they only face two or three during the regular season this year. Over 11.5 The pressure of going perfect may ultimately be too much, but Miami feels like the only major stumbling block and they’ve had to do a lot of retooling on defense. While we probably all underestimated Miami last season, Notre Dame was favored on the road in the lid lifter last season, for whatever that’s worth. The Irish were so perturbed about their CFP snub that they didn’t bother playing a bowl game, but you can tell that everybody has bought in, as the only players of note that left did so for the NFL and not for other schools. My projection is 11.42 wins, and they are favored by 8.5 or more in every game.

## 26. Open Questions / Risks

The guide's *Three Burning Questions for the 2026 Season* *(p. 213)*, with the answers as written:

### Are there any weaknesses on offense?

Carr had a 24/6 TD/INT ratio last season and added three more scores on the ground, though he was hardly the rushing threat that Riley Leonard was. The depth behind Carr is a major worry if something were to happen to him, but he spent most of the spring and summer as the favorite to win the Heisman Trophy. The schedule surely has a lot to do with that, as anything under 11 wins would be a bit of a surprise, so he should be putting up numbers and winning games for a very visible program. While Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price are gone, taking over 2,000 rushing yards and 29 rushing scores with them, Aneyas Williams should be able to keep the bar high at that position. Similarly, while Jordan Faison is the only notable returnee at wide receiver, Jaden Greathouse is back after missing nearly all of last season due to injury. Plus, the offensive line looks very good, including the return of Charles Jagusah. So, in a word, no.

### Are there any weaknesses on defense?

The TL;DR version of this question is one simple word - no. Unlike a lot of premier programs with heavy personnel losses, second- year DC Chris Ash has his top six tacklers back. The Irish were one of 11 teams to hold opponents to fewer than three yards per carry and only eight teams allowed fewer yards on a per-play basis. Notre Dame has had a lot of coaches and players roll through in the past seven years and they’ve only allowed more than 19.7 PPG one time. Hell, they’ve allowed under five yards per play in each of the last three seasons under Freeman. They are +31 in TO margin over the last two seasons, which is one area of concern, but not if Carr takes care of the ball. The defense will go ball-hawking again after securing 21 interceptions last season.

### Anything else?

It feels like I’ve said about all I can say about this team. Notre Dame’s two close losses last season were followed up by a bunch of blowout wins, as they outgained their other 10 opponents by more than 1,800 yards in total and outscored them by nearly 300 points. As long as the Irish avoid cluster injuries, the goal of a perfect season is very attainable, and that includes the CFP as well. It should also be noted that Notre Dame only plays four true road games - Purdue, North Carolina, BYU, and Syracuse. Two of their “road” games are in neutral settings, with one in Green Bay and one in Foxboro. The Irish get an extra week to prepare for Navy’s triple- option with a well-timed bye that comes the week after they play in elevation at BYU.
